# gyro_server_public_ip (Resource)

Public IPv4 of a Gyro Cloud Istanbul (tr-ist-1) server: enabled = false makes the server private-only (reachable from its VPC, a VPC gateway port forward or the web console). Needs a ready private network card (gyro_server_nic) and no additional IPv4. If the VPC gateway NAT is off the server loses internet access; that is refused unless allow_no_egress = true. The address stays reserved: turning it on brings the same IP. Destroying this resource turns the public IP back on. Import: <server_id>.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Private-only database server: reachable from the VPC (and the web console), internet egress through the VPC gateway NAT.
resource "gyro_server_nic" "db" {
  server_id = gyro_server.db.id
  subnet_id = gyro_vpc.uretim.default_subnet_id
}

resource "gyro_server_public_ip" "db" {
  server_id  = gyro_server.db.id
  enabled    = false
  depends_on = [gyro_server_nic.db]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `enabled` (Boolean) false = public IPv4 off (private-only server), true = on. Changed in place.
- `server_id` (Number) tr-ist-1 server id.

### Optional

- `allow_no_egress` (Boolean) Allow turning it off although the server then has no internet access (VPC gateway NAT off).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as server_id.
- `ip` (String) The server's public IPv4 (kept while off).
- `private_ready` (Boolean) The server has a ready private network card.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import gyro_server_public_ip.db 12345
```
